answer: Admission runs through a cedar, an unrelated party whose standing is the voyage it has closed, read from its own signed log, and which forfeits that standing if the ledge it carves is later slashed. A cedar carves one ledge per voyage closed; an operator's tenth identity must occupy a ledge from a cedar of at least ten voyage that has carved nothing for that operator before, and the thousandth needs a thousand. A thousand clones therefore need a thousand separate cedars of a thousand voyage each — a million voyage of earned standing, none of it rentable.
